_comment: The first fifteen minutes, as data. Beats, placements and the conversations they run — docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md is the prose version of this file and the two are meant to be read together.
_comment_tunable: Every distance and speed here is TUNABLE and none of it is a mechanic. The expected feedback is 'the walk to Grandpa is too long' and 'my pal keeps treading on me', and both have to be answerable by editing this file.
_comment_positions: All offsets are metres from the player's spawn point, which playground_world.gd puts on the baked ground at the world origin. Y is never given: everything is stood on the ground by asking the world for its height (docs/decisions/D09), never by a raycast and never by a hand-placed Y that rots the next time the terrain is baked.

grandpa._comment: Far enough that beat 2 is a walk worth taking and the meadow gets to be looked at; near enough that a player who wanders off can find him again. About eight seconds at a sprint, twenty-five at a walk.
grandpa._comment_config: Which block of data/config/art.json his body comes from.

starters._comment: GAME_DESIGN.md 3: three unique starters, Ground/Water/Air, and the two you do not take stay with him. They are standing bodies you walk up to, NOT a menu — docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md calls that decided and load-bearing, and a list box would undo it.
starters._comment_placement: A row in front of Grandpa, on his own facing, so he is behind them and the player approaches all three head-on. Ported from the previous prototype's src/ui/starterPlacement.ts, which had the same job.
starters._comment_spread: Metres between neighbours. Wide enough that the interaction arbiter's nearest-wins rule reads as YOUR choice rather than as the game guessing: at 3.5m apart, standing in front of one puts you at least 3m from either of the others.
starters._comment_prompt: Deliberately tighter than Grandpa's. You have to commit to one by standing in front of it.

follower._comment: How your pal walks with you. It has no locomotion of its own — every value here is turned into a direction and a speed for pal_body.request_move(), the same call the combat AI and your own stick go through.
follower._comment_stop: Well clear of the trainer's 0.4m capsule plus a 0.65m pal. A follower that stands on the player shoves the camera about.
follower._comment_resume: Hysteresis. Equal to stop_distance, the pal oscillates on the boundary and jitters on the spot.
follower._comment_speeds: Walk is under the trainer's 5.0 and run is under the 8.6 sprint on purpose: a pal that can always keep up never has to hurry, and the little burst when it falls behind is most of what makes it read as alive.

encounter._comment: Beat 6-8. The species is not named here: encounter_director.gd already spawns a bramblebun as its peaceful practice pal and this points at that one, so there is one wild creature rather than two standing in the same meadow.
encounter._comment_species: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md: highest catch_rate in species.json (0.55), chosen so the tutorial catch cannot fail twice.

beats._comment: The beat ORDER is the key order of `grandpa_conversations`, and each key's value is the conversation Grandpa runs if you talk to him during that beat. scripts/story/opening_beats.gd reads this; scripts/story/sequence_director.gd holds which one is current.
beats._comment_correction: This previously said the order lived in scripts/story/opening_beats.gd, 'which is code because it is a state machine rather than content'. That file did not exist when the line was written and the order was nowhere at all. The order is content — it is the shape of the first fifteen minutes and it will be argued with — so it stays here, and the code reads it.
beats._comment_free_play: Empty means he has nothing scripted left and his prompt goes quiet rather than repeating his send-off forever. His last line offers feeding; feeding is not built, and inventing a line for it here would be inventing content. Put a conversation id here the day there is one.
beats._comment_named: Not reached by walking up to him. The director starts it the instant the name is confirmed, with `$name` substituted into it.

effects._comment: What a `beat:` effect out of data/dialogue/opening.json means in beat terms. The writer names MOMENTS ('starter_choice'); the state machine names BEATS ('choose'), and the two vocabularies deliberately do not have to match — the dialogue system has no idea what a beat is and should not acquire one. This is the join, and it is data because both sides of it are.

fade._comment: Beat 1 is a fade-in from black rather than an interior. docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md: that saves an entire interior art pass for a beat that lasts forty seconds.
